method: Started from the coordinator's candidate list of CEOs of large, well-known US-listed companies who were pushed out, fired or 'stepped down' under pressure in 2016-2026, plus additions found while researching (CBS, Campbell, Expedia, Gap, FirstEnergy, Ford). For each, located the departure 8-K (Item 5.02) and the next proxy's separation disclosures via EDGAR submissions and full-text search; recorded what the filing says was paid or payable for that departure (basis 'actual') or, where only contract terms or targets exist, 'estimated'. Forfeiture-only cases (for-cause or no-severance exits) are kept when the forfeiture or clawback is quantified or is the story. Stock windows use 10-K Item 5 performance tables or proxy pay-versus-performance tables whose base date and end date both fall inside the CEO tenure (longest such window); graphs printed only as images, or tenures with no in-tenure base date, get stock = null. Candidates with no exit pay (voluntary resignations with nothing paid) are listed in 'rejected'.

cases.exit_words: John G. Stumpf notified Wells Fargo & Company (the “Company”) of his decision to retire as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer and a director of the Company, effective immediately.
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: September 2016: Stumpf and the board agreed he would forfeit all unvested equity, forgo salary during the board's investigation and get no 2016 annual incentive (g233). Wells Fargo's 2017 proxy values the forfeited awards at $41,155,361 (912,739 shares of 2014-2016 Performance Shares and RSRs, at the September 27, 2016 closing price with Performance Shares at target; 'approximately $41 million') (g231, g232). On April 7, 2017 the board 'determined to claw back additional compensation' of 'approximately $28 million (the value at the time of distribution in March 2016 of shares issued to him following vesting of his Performance Share award granted on March 8, 2013)' (g234, April 2017 8-K).
cases.notes: Recorded because the forfeiture and clawback are the story: Wells Fargo says he received 'no severance payments or retirement enhancements' on leaving, other than a part-time driver for security (estimated at under $10,000 a year if used; not used in 2016) plus office space and administrative support to help with the CEO transition and the board's investigation (2017 proxy). Severance and the 2016 bonus are therefore recorded as $0; the driver, office space and administrative support are not valued. Not counted as exit pay: his accrued retirement benefit, paid as an early-retirement benefit (a Cash Balance Plan annuity of $7,335 a month and a Supplemental Cash Balance Plan lump sum of about $24,643,625), which the 2017 proxy says was not enhanced (g236). The proxy notes that, as a retirement-eligible employee, the forfeited RSRs and Performance Shares 'normally would have continued to vest after retirement', and that the 2014 Performance Shares would have paid at 150% of target, so the $41 million at-target figure understates what he gave up. The 8-K's word is 'retire'. Stock: Wells Fargo's 10-Ks incorporate a 'Stock Performance' section of the annual report that is not in the EDGAR exhibit text (checked the FY2012, FY2015 and FY2016 filings; the ARS was filed on paper), and pay-versus-performance tables did not exist before 2022, so there is no verifiable in-tenure $100 table; stock is null.

cases.exit_words: Mark Fields has elected to retire from the Company effective August 1, 2017, and has resigned from the Board of Directors, effective immediately.
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: The Committee let him keep the 2017 Time-Based Unit grant and the annual Performance Unit grant, "however, the $2.5 million strategic incentive grant was cancelled."
cases.notes: Ford's 2018 proxy prints a table of "the incremental compensation and benefits paid to him as a result of his retirement": Incentive Bonus Plan $350,000 (bonus prorated to August 1 rather than his June 1 retirement date), Performance Units $4,686,566, Restricted Stock Units $3,154,420 and Evaluation Vehicles $9,404, Total $8,200,390 (equity valued at $11.41, Ford's June 1, 2017 close). The equity field holds only the Performance Units figure because the verifier needs one printed number per field; the $3,154,420 of retained 2017 RSUs is included in the total. pension_deferred is the present value of his Select Retirement Plan (SRP) benefit, $5,334,183, a voluntary separation program that adds three years of age and service; his separation agreement included participation in it. The total, $13,534,573, is the proxy's $8,200,390 plus the SRP present value. It is not printed in the filing. Pension figures from his regular plans (GRP, SERP, GRP-BEP, ESAP) are not counted. Tenure start is July 1, 2014, when he became CEO; the end date is May 19, 2017, the day the proxy says Hackett became CEO. The 8-K is dated May 22. Stock window: Ford's FY2019 10-K table, $100 invested December 31, 2014, read at December 31, 2016, the last fiscal year end of his tenure.

cases.exit_words: resigned from his position as Chief Executive Officer and as a member of lululemon's board of directors, effective immediately
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: No continued or accelerated vesting: all unvested options, RSUs and performance-based RSUs were forfeited, the awards granted in fiscal 2017 were forfeited, and he did not earn the fiscal 2017 non-equity incentive (2018 proxy: "All unvested performance-based restricted stock units and restricted stock units were forfeited.").
cases.notes: Under the separation agreement and release, lululemon agreed to pay a $3,350,000 lump sum plus $1,650,000 in 18 monthly installments, in exchange for a release of claims, a 24-month non-solicitation period, a covenant not to sue and future cooperation. The 2018 proxy's termination table prints the $5,000,000 as severance and as the total (scenario 'Voluntary'), payable as $4,280,769 in fiscal 2018 and $719,231 in fiscal 2019. The company's press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) says he resigned and that 'Mr. Potdevin fell short of these standards of conduct'. The 2018 proxy says his fiscal 2017 total compensation would have been $7,208,053 had he earned the non-equity incentive. Stock: the fiscal 2018 10-K performance table starts Feb 2, 2014 (two weeks after he became CEO on Jan 20, 2014); Jan 28, 2018 is the last fiscal year-end before his Feb 2, 2018 resignation, which gives the longest in-tenure window.

cases.exit_words: Following a review, which took place prior to the release of the Company’s third-quarter results, the Board initiated a dialogue with Denise M. Morrison, the then-President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, expressing its dissatisfaction with the performance and execution of the business. After further discussion with the Board, Ms. Morrison agreed with the Board that she would retire, effective as of May 18, 2018.
cases.notes: Her May 17, 2018 retirement agreement paid two years of base salary ($2,304,000) and two years of insurance benefits ($29,697), plus reimbursement of up to $30,000 in legal fees (not separately quantified). It also let her collect her fiscal 2018 annual bonus without proration; the Summary Compensation Table shows $0 non-equity incentive for fiscal 2018, so none was paid. equity is the $6,212,645 value (at $40.94, the July 27, 2018 close) of outstanding long-term awards that keep vesting under retirement treatment. She qualified for that treatment on age and service, so it reflects the plans' standard retirement terms rather than a special grant. The 8-K says Morrison "chose to retire"; exit_words quote the proxy's account of the board dialogue. The 2018 proxy is a DEFC14A (contested solicitation, Third Point). Stock window: the FY2017 10-K, $100 invested July 27, 2012 through July 28, 2017, inside her tenure (CEO since August 2011).

cases.role: Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer
cases.exit_words: On September 9, 2018 (the “Termination Date”), pursuant to the separation agreement, Leslie Moonves resigned as a director of the Company and as Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer, effectively immediately.
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: CBS put $120 million into a grantor trust for him. The board later "determined that there were grounds to terminate his employment with the Company for cause", and after the arbitration was dismissed in May 2021, "The assets of the grantor trust will revert to the Company in their entirety." He also forfeited $34,475,647 of 2018 stock awards and received no 2018 bonus.
cases.notes: The 2019 proxy's table of separation payments lists Moonves at 0 in every column (salary continuation, bonus continuation, incremental pension, insurance, LTI vesting), marked "Subject to binding arbitration"; recorded as $0. The only exit benefit not valued is the Separation Agreement's office and security services for up to two years. He also agreed to perform transition advisory services "without any compensation or benefits". His deferred compensation balance was paid out in 2018; that is money already earned and is not counted. The $20 million CBS committed to #MeToo-related charities went to charities, not to him. exit_type is "resigned" because the filing says he resigned; the board's for-cause determination came on December 17, 2018. Stock window: CBS's FY2017 10-K, Class B common, $100 invested December 31, 2012 through December 31, 2017, the last fiscal year end before his exit.

cases.exit_words: a change in leadership occurred under which our former Chairman and CEO, John Flannery, was replaced by Larry Culp
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: GE's 2019 proxy: his February 2018 PSU grant 'was modified in connection with his departure, at which point 466,667 of the original 800,000 PSUs were cancelled'; the 2016 PSUs he kept eligibility for were later cancelled for missed targets ('ultimately no payment was made for the 2016 PSUs'), and no 2018 bonus was paid (g225, g221).
cases.notes: GE's 2019 proxy describes his separation agreement: severance of $4,250,000 paid over 12 months, subject to a 12-month non-compete; accelerated vesting of options and RSUs granted before September 30, 2017 that would have vested through December 31, 2020, with options exercisable to December 31, 2020; continued eligibility for 333,333 of his 2018 PSUs; and vesting of his accrued Supplementary Pension Plan benefit (payable from age 60, with an extra year of service credited for the severance period). Equity $3,051,717 is the proxy's 'Upon Involuntary Termination' figure for Flannery, the intrinsic value of options, RSUs and PSUs that vested or became exercisable under the separation agreement, measured at GE's December 31, 2018 stock price with performance assumed achieved. pension_deferred $21,160,674 is the present value at December 31, 2018 of his Supplementary Pension Plan benefit, which the proxy says vested under the separation agreement; he left at 56, before the plan's age-60 retirement point. That counts the whole present value of a benefit the agreement vested (including the extra credited year), not just the enhancement; GE's broad-based GE Pension Plan value ($1,718,825) is excluded. The pension table notes the executives 'are not entitled to receive these amounts in a lump sum'. The proxy says the 2016-2018 LTPA was payable pro rata but paid nothing. Total = 4,250,000 + 3,051,717 + 21,160,674 = 28,462,391 (sum of printed parts). The proxy's Potential Termination table puts his payments in the 'Upon Involuntary Termination' column, whose footnote covers separation 'without cause' or, 'in the case of Mr. Flannery, his separation agreement' (g228), which is the basis for exit_type. The October 2018 8-K says he 'resigned from the GE Board on September 30, 2018'. Stock: his CEO tenure (August 1, 2017-September 30, 2018) contains only one fiscal year-end and GE had no pay-versus-performance table then, so no performance table has both ends in tenure; stock is null.

cases.exit_words: Timothy J. Sloan has stepped down as Chief Executive Officer and President, and as a director of the Company. He also will retire from the Company on June 30, 2019.
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: The HRC 'exercised its discretion to cancel the Performance Share award in the amount of $15 million granted to Mr. Sloan in February 2019' (311,788 target shares, shown at $16,774,173 at the December 31, 2019 price), and he received no 2019 annual incentive (g244, g241).
cases.notes: No severance. Wells Fargo says he got 'normal retirement treatment', under which his outstanding equity awards kept vesting on schedule after he retired (otherwise 'Performance Shares and RSRs forfeit immediately' for employees who are not retirement-eligible). Values from the 2020 proxy's Outstanding Equity Awards at Fiscal Year-End 2019 table, at the $53.80 December 31, 2019 close: RSRs $404,340 (balance subject to regulatory approval), 2017 Performance Shares $17,852,214 (performance period ended December 31, 2019, certified at 117% of target; payment to executive officers delayed), and 2018 Performance Shares at target $13,357,406 (to vest, if earned, in Q1 2021). Also counted: a retiree medical insurance subsidy valued at $35,472 and $5,105 for a part-time driver after retirement under the Chairman/CEO Post-Retirement Policy (which also gave office space and non-dedicated administrative help, not quantified). The equity field holds the 2017 Performance Shares figure and benefits_other the medical subsidy; total = 404,340 + 17,852,214 + 13,357,406 + 35,472 + 5,105 = 31,654,537 (sum of printed parts; the filing prints no total). Later Wells Fargo proxies (2021) do not mention him, so the final payouts are not confirmed in filings. The cancelled 2019 award is excluded from the total. The 8-K says he 'stepped down'; the 2020 proxy says he 'resigned as CEO and President on March 28, 2019 and retired from the Company on June 30, 2019'. Stock: Wells Fargo's 10-Ks of this period print no performance-graph table (they incorporate a non-EDGAR annual report section), and its pay-versus-performance tables start at December 31, 2019, after his tenure, so stock is null.

cases.exit_words: will leave the Company effective June 30, 2019 to focus on other projects as a Partner of 3G Capital; In June 2019, Mr. Hees stepped down as CEO
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: Per the 2020 proxy, Mr. Hees forfeited his 2017 and 2018 RSUs and 2018 PSUs pursuant to his separation agreement (g408).
cases.notes: Severance terms approved June 5, 2019 under the Kraft Heinz Severance Pay Plan and his separation agreement: 12 months of base salary plus a pro-rata 2019 bonus assuming 85% performance (g401). severance_cash = 'Separation Pay' column of the 2019 All Other Compensation table ($1,000,000; g402). bonus = 2019 Non-Equity Incentive Plan Compensation in the Summary Compensation Table ($1,084,000; g403), which footnote (2) of the grants table describes as the pro-rata bonus assuming 85% performance (g404). equity = value realized on vesting of 25,880 shares ($803,315; g405): 60% of the 2016 Matching RSUs, 40% of the 2017 Matching RSUs plus accrued dividends, which vested on prorated schedules 'as a result of his departure' (g406, g407), valued at $31.04, the close on the last trading day before his June 28, 2019 separation date. Not quantified: options that vested on prorated schedules at his departure (e.g. 60% of the 8/20/15 grant at a $74.25 strike and 80% of the 2/12/15 option-match at $30.46), which were at or near/under water at the $31.04 separation-date price. The 2019 All Other Compensation total ($1,212,904) also includes $149,457 of relocation (2017 house sale), 401(k) match and dividend equivalents, which are not counted here. Total is the sum of the three recorded parts (not printed in the filing). Tenure: CEO of Kraft Heinz from the July 2, 2015 merger; the 2020 proxy says Mr. Patricio succeeded him as CEO on June 25, 2019 (tenure_end set to June 24, 2019); his separation date was June 28, 2019. Stock: FY2018 10-K performance graph, $100 invested July 6, 2015 (first trading day) to December 28, 2018, both inside his tenure; no later in-tenure year-end exists. exit_type 'other': the filings describe the exit as leaving 'to focus on other projects as a Partner of 3G Capital' and 'stepped down', while paying severance under a plan the proxy describes as covering involuntary terminations.

cases.exit_words: terminated by the Company without cause
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: In August 2020 McDonald's sued him in the Delaware Court of Chancery "to recover compensation and severance benefits that would not have been retained by Mr. Easterbrook had he been terminated for cause," saying that had the Board known information found later, "it would not have approved the terms of the Separation Agreement" (8-K, 2020-08-10). The December 16, 2021 settlement release (8-K Ex. 99.1): "Under the settlement, Mr. Easterbrook has returned equity awards and cash, with a current value of over $105 million, which he would have forfeited had he been truthful at the time of his termination and, as a result, been terminated for cause."
cases.notes: Pay is what the 2020 proxy says he was entitled to on his November 1, 2019 termination: separation payment $700,000 (severance_cash), pro-rated 2019 STIP $3,063,872 (bonus), outplacement $25,000 (benefits_other) and a $2,516 continued health subsidy. benefits_other holds only the printed outplacement figure; total ($3,791,388) is my sum of all four printed parts including the $2,516 health subsidy, so total_is_stated is false. Equity: per the separation agreement and 2020 proxy, options that would have vested within three years kept vesting and stayed exercisable three years, and PRSUs were pro-rated and left outstanding; the proxy says it could not value PRSUs and gives no dollar figure for the continued vesting, so equity is null. Those continued-vesting awards are what the later lawsuit and settlement recovered: the settlement says he returned equity and cash worth over $105 million (printed only as '$105 million', so not recorded as a pay figure). The exit was recorded as 'without cause' at the time; the 2020 lawsuit says he would have been terminated for cause had the Board known the later-found facts. Stock: FY2020 10-K performance table, base 12/31/2015 (he became CEO 3/1/2015) to 12/31/2018, the latest year-end before his November 1, 2019 exit; MCD $163 vs S&P 500 Index $130 (the table also shows DJIA companies $144). No 10-K table has a base date earlier in his tenure.

cases.exit_words: Mr. Peck was terminated without cause from the position of President & CEO, Gap Inc. in November 2019
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: "As a result of Mr. Peck’s termination, the restricted stock units granted to him in 2018 covering 345,303 shares were canceled. In addition, his fiscal 2017-2019, fiscal 2018-2020 and fiscal 2019-2021 LGP shares were canceled and his fiscal 2019 bonus was not earned."
cases.notes: The 2020 proxy's "2019 Post-Termination Payments" table shows what he is eligible to receive: salary continuation for 18 months ($2,325,000), health benefits ($21,851), financial counseling ($22,950) and stock award vesting acceleration ($1,380,491, valued at the $17.74 close on November 15, 2019), for a printed total of $3,750,292. benefits_other holds the health-benefit figure only; the financial counseling is included in the stated total. The 8-K said he "is stepping down" and would also get "certain retirement benefits based on the stock grant agreements". Excluded: his deferred compensation, which he was entitled to on termination anyway. Stock window: the FY2020 10-K table, $100 invested January 30, 2016 (the first fiscal year end after he became CEO on February 1, 2015) through February 2, 2019, the last fiscal year end before his exit.

cases.exit_words: Chief Executive Officer Mark Okerstrom and Chief Financial Officer Alan Pickerill resigned from the Company at the request of the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”), effective immediately.
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: On termination, "51,930 RSUs and 345,946 stock options were forfeited"; he received no 2019 cash bonus.
cases.notes: The 2020 proxy treats this as a qualifying termination. equity is the $5,839,227 value of 54,278 RSUs whose vesting was accelerated at termination. The $1,420,219 value of 887,804 options that vested and became exercisable is also accelerated equity; it is included in the total but not in the equity field, because the verifier needs a single printed figure per field. benefits_other is the $36,000 COBRA payment. Salary continuation runs "through the longer of the end of the term of the employment agreement (subject to a maximum of 36 months for Mr. Okerstrom only) and 12 months," offset by other earnings. The filings quantify only the first installment ($19,231 in 2019), so severance_cash is null and the full amount is excluded from the total. His base salary was $1,000,000 in 2018. The total, $7,295,446 = $5,839,227 + $1,420,219 + $36,000, is our sum and is not printed. Stock is null: the 10-K performance graphs (e.g., FY2022, base December 31, 2017) print no values, and pay-versus-performance tables start after his tenure.

cases.exit_words: on December 22, 2019, Dennis A. Muilenburg resigned as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a director
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: Boeing's 2020 proxy: 'Of the awards granted in 2019, Mr. Muilenburg forfeited 6,111 unvested RSUs, 5,614 unvested PBRSUs (calculated assuming target performance), and unvested performance awards with a target value of $4,830,867 in connection with his retirement in December 2019.' He received no 2019 annual incentive (no NEO did) and no severance or separation payment (g200, g201, g203).
cases.notes: No severance was paid. Boeing's 2020 proxy says that, because he was retirement-eligible under pre-existing plan terms, he vested on exit in pro-rated long-term incentive awards valued as of his retirement date at $8,542,853 (RSUs), $12,691,088 (PBRSUs, at target except the 2017-2019 PBRSUs at their 175% payout) and $13,077,900 (performance award units, at target), and also vested in Career Shares and MDSUs valued at $4,330,463 as of his separation date. The equity field holds only the RSU figure (the one component fully fixed at retirement); total = 8,542,853 + 12,691,088 + 13,077,900 + 4,330,463 = 38,642,304, a sum of the filing's printed parts that the filing never prints. PBRSU and performance-award-unit payouts depended on later performance, so their final value may differ. The Career Shares/MDSUs were stock units earned before he became CEO (per the proxy) that vested at separation; Boeing's later proxies list Career Share vesting as an exit benefit, so they are counted here. Not counted as exit pay: his accrued pension (DB SERP present value $15,272,729, PVP $1,181,929) and deferred-compensation balances, which the proxy reports as ordinary accrued benefits. The proxy's own summary line reads that he 'was not paid any severance or other benefits in connection with his retirement' (g203). The 8-K says he 'resigned'; the proxy calls the departure his 'retirement'. Tenure start is July 1, 2015 per the June 2015 8-K. Stock window: Boeing's 10-Ks of this period print no performance-graph table and pay-versus-performance tables start at a December 31, 2019 base, so no table has both ends inside July 2015-December 22, 2019; stock is null.

cases.exit_words: Mr. Strah’s appointment to Acting CEO followed the determination by the Independent Review Committee of the Board of Directors (“Independent Review Committee”) to terminate Mr. Jones as the Company’s Chief Executive Officer effective October 29, 2020.
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: "As a result of Mr. Jones’ termination, and due to the determination that Mr. Jones violated certain Company policies and its code of conduct, all grants, awards and compensation under the Company’s short-term incentive compensation program and long-term incentive compensation program with respect to Mr. Jones that were outstanding on the date of termination have been forfeited."
cases.notes: The 2021 proxy says "no severance benefits were provided to him" and his 2020 short-term incentive payout was forfeited, so severance and bonus are recorded as $0. His 2020 stock awards had a maximum grant-date value of $12,057,667 and were forfeited; that is a grant value, not a realized amount. exit_type is "other": the filing says the committee determined "to terminate" him and that he violated Company policies, but it does not use the words "for cause". The termination followed the company's internal review tied to the HB 6 government investigations. Stock is null: the FY2020 10-K graph (base December 31, 2015) prints no values, and earlier 10-K bases (December 31, 2014) fall one day before his tenure.

cases.exit_words: the Company's and Mr. Foley's mutual determination that Mr. Foley would step down from his position as our Executive Chair
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: Per the FY2023 proxy, option awards that would have remained unvested beyond the 12-month acceleration window "for which vesting was not accelerated, were forfeited."
cases.notes: Foley was replaced as CEO on February 9, 2022 and became Executive Chair; the parachute was paid when he left that role and the Board on September 12, 2022 under a Founder Transition Agreement (Severance Plan benefits plus 18 rather than 12 months of health coverage and option exercisability extended to June 30, 2025). Figures are from the FY2023 proxy Summary Compensation Table (actual): All Other Compensation $1,083,187 = $1,000,000 base salary continuation (severance_cash, also stated in the 2022 proxy) plus Company-paid health continuation including a $46,002 tax gross-up (tax_gross_up); the remaining $37,185 of health premiums is in total but not in a field. Option Awards $35,327,075 (equity) is the ASC 718 incremental fair value of extending his options' exercise period to June 30, 2025, which the proxy attributes to his termination; the proxy says the 12-month accelerated vesting itself had no incremental fair value. This is an accounting value, not cash realized. total = 1,083,187 + 35,327,075 = $36,410,262 (my sum; total_is_stated false). Not counted: FY2023 salary of $234,615 for July 1 - Sept 12, 2022. The 2022 proxy's hypothetical June 30, 2022 table showed $1,207,462 for a non-CIC termination. Tenure start is given as 2012: filings say he founded and led the company 'since its inception' and that Peloton was formed in 2012. Stock: the only in-tenure table is the FY2023 proxy pay-versus-performance table (base June 30, 2020; the FY2021 column June 30, 2021 is the last in his CEO tenure): PTON $215 vs Nasdaq Computer Index $150. The table has no S&P 500 column. Peloton's 10-K performance graphs (base Sept 26, 2019 IPO) are images with no printed values.

cases.exit_words: will be stepping down from his role and as a member of the Company's Board of Directors
cases.clawback_or_forfeiture: Upon his departure, Mr. Frisk was not eligible to receive a fiscal year 2023 annual cash incentive award and he forfeited all of his unvested equity awards (g427).
cases.notes: Separation agreement dated May 17, 2022 (8-K exhibit 10.01). severance_cash = $6,890,000 separation payments, two times base salary plus target annual cash incentive at 165% of salary (g422). benefits_other = the $238,000 lump sum the 8-K describes as reimbursing relocation, 18 months of COBRA and outplacement (g421); the 2023 proxy splits it into $38,000 COBRA/outplacement and $200,000 relocation from the Baltimore area (g423). consulting = $1,300,000 aggregate consulting fee under the consulting agreement attached to the separation agreement, payable in four $325,000 quarterly installments through September 4, 2023 (g424); the FY2023 proxy reports $758,333 of consulting fees received between September 2022 and March 2023 (g425). He also remained an employee-advisor from June 1 to September 1, 2022 (salary for that period not separately disclosed) and received tax-preparation services for 2021 and 2022 (FY2023 All Other Compensation includes $52,900 for tax services and a related tax gross-up; not counted). Excluded: $102,925 of accrued but unused paid time off. The proxy's 'Separation on September 1, 2022' row prints cash severance $7,288,476, benefits $38,000, total $7,326,476 (g426); that row includes accrued PTO and is not used as the total. Total = 6,890,000 + 238,000 + 1,300,000, computed (not printed). Stock: the only Item 5 table with a base date inside his tenure (CEO January 1, 2020 to May 31, 2022, per the PvP footnote g428) is the FY2026 10-K graph based December 31, 2020; its last in-tenure point is March 31, 2022 (Class A stock $99.12 vs S&P 500 $122.79). Alternative under a looser reading: the FY2025 10-K graph is based December 31, 2019, the last trading day before he became CEO, and shows Class A $78.79 vs S&P 500 $145.38 at March 31, 2022 (g432, g433). exit_type 'other': the filings say he would 'step down'; the separation agreement superseded the severance he was otherwise eligible for under the executive severance policy.

cases.exit_words: ceased serving as President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company and as a member of the Board of Directors; eligible for separation payments and benefits provided upon a termination of employment without "cause"
cases.notes: Separation and Release Agreement dated June 27, 2022 (exhibit 10.3 to the 10-Q filed September 30, 2022). severance_cash = $6,765,000, two times the sum of annual salary ($1,230,000) and full fiscal 2022 target bonus ($2,152,500), payable in ratable installments over 24 months (g462, g465); the FY2022 Summary Compensation Table reports it in All Other Compensation (g464). benefits_other = a separate lump sum cash payment of $202,192 under the separation agreement; the filing does not say what it is for (g463). Not quantified: COBRA at active-employee rates for up to 24 months. equity = null: his outstanding RSUs and PSUs stayed subject to the award agreements, which give a prorated portion continued vesting on the original dates after a termination without cause (g467); at the February 24, 2023 close of $1.53 the FY-end table values them at $586,301 (383,203 RSUs) and $386,437 (252,573 PSUs at target) (g466), but most were scheduled to vest on or after June 8, 2023, after the company filed for Chapter 11 on April 23, 2023 (g469), so no realized value is recorded. The separation agreement anticipated that a Chapter 11 rejection could stop the monthly severance installments (g468); no filing reports how much of the $6,765,000 was actually paid before or after the petition. Total = 6,765,000 + 202,192, computed (not printed). Stock = null: the FY2022 10-K performance graph is an image based February 25, 2017 (before his tenure), no pay-versus-performance table was filed for FY2022 (10-K Part III, filed June 2023), and earlier 10-K graphs are also based before November 2019, so no table has a base date inside his tenure.

cases.exit_words: The Company exercised its right to terminate without cause the employment of Robert A. Chapek as Chief Executive Officer.
cases.notes: Cash figures come from the 2024 proxy, which states that Mr. Chapek received these cash termination payments in fiscal 2023: $6,527,397 in remaining base salary through the scheduled June 30, 2025 expiration of his employment agreement (severance_cash) and $1,027,397 as a pro-rated fiscal 2023 target bonus (bonus). The 2023 proxy says these payments were conditioned on his completing a post-employment consulting agreement; no separate consulting fee is disclosed. Equity: the 2024 proxy says all his equity awards continued to vest after termination, but it discloses no actual value. The 2023 proxy's hypothetical end-of-fiscal-2022 table assigns $12,657,435 (at the $94.33 Sept 30, 2022 close) to the enhanced vesting. The same footnote notes that, because he was retirement-eligible (age 60, 10 years' service), all of those awards except the fiscal 2022 grants would have kept vesting anyway had he retired. The exit-triggered part of that estimate is therefore unknown, so equity is null and the $12,657,435 is not counted. rejected.name: Andrew Witty
rejected.reason: Filings describe a voluntary exit with no exit payment. The May 2025 8-K says he notified the Company of 'his decision to step down', and the 2026 proxy says he chose to 'voluntarily step down from the position of CEO, effective May 12, 2025 and accordingly, no severance is payable' and that he 'was not entitled to any payments during the fiscal year in connection with his stepping down'. He stayed on as a senior advisor (an employee) with base salary cut from $1,500,000 to $500,000. Advisor-period pay is not separately quantified, and he is no longer eligible for incentive payouts or stock awards. His Feb 20, 2025 performance share award (target value $11,500,000) was cancelled with his consent on June 2, 2025. No quantified parachute; a voluntary cancellation is not a clawback, so the case is not recorded (UNH CIK 0000731766; Witty reporting-owner CIK 0001711304; 2026 DEF 14A accession 0001104659-26-046125).
